questions.q: Which shortcut **inserts a hyperlink** in Word or Excel?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+K** opens the hyperlink dialog (K sits next to L for 'link' on the keyboard).

questions.q: Which shortcut makes selected text **bold**?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+B** = bold, Ctrl+I = italic, Ctrl+U = underline — the initial letters.

questions.q: Your home Wi-Fi router joins your family's devices to the Internet. In networking terms it is acting as a —
options: Router connecting a LAN to a WAN
questions.solution: The home box routes between your **LAN** and the ISP's network (**WAN/Internet**), besides serving Wi-Fi.

questions.q: A photographer needs a **64-GB SD card** that stores individual video files larger than 4 GB and still works in cameras. The best format is —
questions.solution: **exFAT** (extended FAT) removes FAT32's 4-GB file limit and stays light enough for cameras and flash media — the standard choice for large SD cards.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Sita said to Gita, "You are late for the class."
options: Sita told Gita that she is late for the class.
Sita told Gita that she was late for the class.
Sita told Gita that you were late for the class.
Sita told Gita that they were late for the class.
questions.solution: you is the listener, so it becomes **she** (Gita); are steps to **was**. 'She is late' skips the rung; keeping 'you' leaves the quote half-direct; 'they' breaks the number — one listener, singular.
questions.shortcut: 2nd person borrows the listener: you → she/he.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A black sheep
options: a member who brings disgrace to the family or group
the youngest child in a family
questions.solution: Black = disgrace. *A black sheep* is the member whose conduct shames the family or group.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I found ___ one-rupee coin on the pavement.
questions.solution: 'One' begins with the consonant sound 'wu' → **a** one-rupee coin.

questions.q: If the scheme described in the second paragraph spreads widely, which of the following is most likely to happen?
options: Farmers will stop growing crops altogether
Less groundwater will be pumped out, since spare power can earn money instead
Power companies will stop buying electricity from farmers
Diesel pumps will become popular again
questions.solution: The scheme lets farmers sell spare electricity 'instead of using it to pump more water'. If many farmers join, less extra pumping will happen, so less groundwater will be drawn. Nothing suggests farmers stop farming; the scheme is the power company buying electricity, so it stopping is the opposite; there is no reason to return to paid diesel.
questions.shortcut: State the passage's rule (spare power → money, not pumping) and apply it to 'many farmers'.
questions.passage:
When Harish replaced his diesel pump with a solar one, his monthly fuel bill fell to zero. For the first time, he could water his fields in the afternoon without worrying about cost, and he did — often for longer than the crop needed. Two years later, the water in his borewell had dropped by several metres.

His neighbours noticed. Some of them have now joined a scheme under which farmers can sell spare solar electricity to the power company instead of using it to pump more water. Harish says the payment is small but steady. 'Earlier, extra sunshine meant extra pumping,' he says. 'Now it means extra money.'

questions.q: Which allotrope of carbon **conducts electricity**?
questions.solution: **Graphite** has free electrons between its layers — used as electrodes. Diamond is an insulator despite being the hardest substance.

questions.q: **Servants of India Society** (1905), which trained dedicated public workers, was founded by —
questions.solution: **Gokhale** founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 — he was also Gandhi's acknowledged political guru.

questions.q: Which single European river flows through the greatest number of capital cities?
questions.solution: The **Danube** passes through **Vienna (Austria), Bratislava (Slovakia), Budapest (Hungary) and Belgrade (Serbia)** - four capitals; the Volga is Europe's longest river but has no capital on it.

questions.q: **Gitanjali**, for which its author received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913, is a collection of —
questions.solution: **Gitanjali** ('Song Offerings') is Tagore's collection of poems; he was the **first Asian** to win a Nobel Prize.

questions.q:
Production of cars (in thousands) by four companies:

| Year | P | Q | R | S |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 120 | 90 | 150 | 80 |
| 2020 | 135 | 110 | 145 | 95 |
| 2021 | 150 | 105 | 160 | 100 |
| 2022 | 140 | 125 | 170 | 110 |
| 2023 | 165 | 130 | 175 | 120 |

Which company showed the highest percentage increase in production from 2019 to 2023?
questions.shortcut: P has the biggest absolute rise (45) but the biggest base too; S doubles half-way (40 on 80).

questions.q: A vegetable vendor sells at the cost price but uses a weight of 750 g for a kilogram. His gain per cent is:
questions.shortcut: Every 3 parts given earn 1 part extra.

questions.q: A and B together take 12 days, B and C together 15 days, and A and C together 20 days for the same work. A alone can do it in:
questions.solution:
Trio rate $= \frac12\left(\frac1{12}+\frac1{15}+\frac1{20}\right) = \frac12 \times \frac{5+4+3}{60} = \frac{1}{10}$.
A $=$ trio $-(B+C) = \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{30}$ → 30 days.

questions.q: The minimum value of $\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta$ ($\theta$ acute) is:
questions.solution: With $x = \tan^2\theta$: $x + \frac1x \ge 2$, equality at $x = 1$ i.e. $\theta = 45^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $2$ at $45^\circ$. Trap: $0$ — a positive term and its reciprocal cannot both vanish.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**LETTER, BALLOON, COFFEE, GARDEN**
questions.solution: No common meaning, so check spelling. LETTER has TT, BALLOON has LL and OO, COFFEE has FF and EE - each has a **double letter**. GARDEN has none → **GARDEN**.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**3   4   10**

**5   2   12**

**6   5   ?**
questions.solution: a + b gives 7 and 7, not 10 and 12 — the first number counts twice. Rule: third = 2 × first + second: 6 + 4 = 10 ✓, 10 + 2 = 12 ✓. So 12 + 5 = **17**. (16 doubles the wrong number.)
questions.shortcut: Output just above a + b by exactly one input → that input is doubled.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**12   23   53**

**31   14   54**

**21   32   ?**
questions.solution: Reverse each input, then add: 21 + 32 = 53 ✓; 13 + 41 = 54 ✓. So 12 + 23 = **35**. (53 adds the unreversed inputs — which is exactly row 1's output, a planted trap.)
questions.shortcut: Outputs look like sums of flipped numbers → reverse first.

questions.q: Which word will look **exactly the same** in its water image?
questions.solution: Water keeps the order, so a word looks unchanged if every letter is in B C D E H I K O X. **BOXED** uses only these letters. BOXER has R; MIXED has M; FIXED has F.
